settings.title: Nil T2 Filing for Numbered Holding Corporations

settings.editor:
A numbered holding corporation is incorporated to hold something rather than to trade: shares in an operating company, a parcel of land, a portfolio, or nothing at all while the owner decides what comes next. It has a number for a name because it was never given one, which is why so many sit quiet for years. Quiet is not the same as closed. The corporation exists until it is dissolved, and paragraph 150(1)(a) makes the T2 due every year it exists.

The question is never whether the return is due. It is whether the year was nil. A holding corporation that received no dividend, earned no interest, collected no rent and disposed of nothing has a nil year, and that return is prepared, CPA reviewed, signed on a T183CORP and transmitted electronically for $300.00 plus HST per tax year. A holding corporation that received any of those has income, and this is not the service for it.

settings.title: When a Numbered Holding Corporation Is Not Nil

settings.description_text: A dividend from the operating company is income to the holding corporation. The year is not nil, whatever was done with the money.
Interest on a balance, a term deposit or a loan to a related company is income. A few dollars of it still makes the year not nil.
A corporation holding property that collects rent is a rental corporation for the year. It is not nil and files a full T2.
A sale of shares, land or any capital property puts a gain or loss in the year. The year is not nil even where the gain is zero.

settings.editor:
This matters more for holding corporations than for any other kind, because the thing a holding corporation holds tends to pay something. A single dividend cheque, one interest posting on a bank statement or one month of rent moves the year out of nil and into an ordinary corporate return with income to report.

Where that is the year you have, Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation prepares it at gondaliyacpa.ca for $350.00 plus HST per year. The nil service here is for the years in which the holding corporation genuinely did nothing, and those are usually the unfiled ones.

settings.title: Which T2 Schedules a Numbered Holding Corporation Files

settings.editor:
ScheduleWhat it reportsOn a nil yearWhy
Schedule 100Balance sheet informationRequiredA holding corporation holds something, so the balance sheet is never empty. Shares, a loan to a shareholder or share capital alone makes Schedule 100 required.
Schedule 125Income statement informationRequiredFiled with Schedule 100. It reports nil revenue and nil expenses for the year rather than being left out.
Schedule 141Notes checklistRequiredAccompanies Schedules 100 and 125 and records who prepared the financial information and on what basis.
Schedule 50Shareholder informationRequiredEvery shareholder holding 10% or more of any class is listed. A single-shareholder numbered corporation still files it.
Schedule 24First-time filer informationFirst return onlyFiled on the corporation’s first T2 after incorporation, then not again.
Schedule 8Capital cost allowanceOnly with depreciable propertyA holding corporation that owns no depreciable property does not file it. One that holds a building does.

Source: the schedule requirements the Canada Revenue Agency sets for a T2 return, read against the facts of a holding corporation with no activity in the year. Last reviewed November 19, 2026.

settings.title_text: The GIFI Trio Is Not Optional Here
settings.description_text: An operating corporation with truly nothing on its books may omit Schedules 100, 125 and 141. A holding corporation rarely can.

settings.title_text: Schedule 50 Lists One Name or Many
settings.description_text: The 10% test applies per class of share. A sole shareholder is still a shareholder and still appears.
A corporation catching up several unfiled years files Schedule 24 with the earliest of them, not with the most recent.

settings.html:
The year is nil

  • No dividend was received from any corporation it holds shares in
  • No interest was posted on any account, deposit or inter-company loan
  • No rent was collected on property it owns
  • Nothing was sold, transferred or otherwise disposed of
  • No expense was claimed, including management or accounting fees

The year is not nil

  • A dividend arrived, even one reinvested or left on account
  • A bank or investment account paid interest of any amount
  • Property it holds produced rent for any part of the year
  • Shares, land or equipment changed hands, at a gain, a loss or neither
  • The corporation paid anything it intends to deduct

Due either way

  • The T2 return itself, for every year the corporation exists
  • A T183CORP signed by an authorised signing officer, one per tax year
  • Schedule 50 listing every shareholder at 10% or more
  • The federal or provincial annual return, which is a separate filing
  • Dissolution, before the obligation to file finally ends

settings.title: Nil T2 Filing for Holding Corporations Across Canada

settings.editor:
Numbered holding corporations are filed the same way wherever the registered office sits, because the return is prepared and transmitted electronically from end to end. There is nothing to print, nothing to post and nothing to sign in person.

Where the corporation was incorporated changes the registry, not the return. An Ontario corporation answers to the Ontario Business Registry, and corporations in British Columbia, Alberta, Quebec and Saskatchewan each answer to their own. The T2 itself is federal and identical in all of them. Within Ontario, a corporation registered in Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton or Ottawa is filed on the same terms and at the same price as one anywhere else in the country.

Two provinces add a return the federal T2 does not cover. A Quebec corporation also files the CO-17 and an Alberta corporation also files the AT1. Both are separate provincial returns, and neither is included in the $300.00 plus HST fee.

settings.title: Nil T2 Filing FAQs for Numbered Holding Corporations

items.item_title: Does a numbered holding corporation with no activity still file a T2?
Is a holding company that receives dividends nil?
My holding corporation only holds shares in my operating company. Is that year nil?
Which schedules does a nil holding corporation file?
Can a holding corporation skip the GIFI schedules?
How many unfiled years can be filed at once?
Does a numbered corporation need a name before it can file?
What happens to a holding corporation that never filed?
Is the T183CORP signed once or once per year?
What if the holding corporation is being wound up?

settings.editor: Yes. Paragraph 150(1)(a) makes the return due for every tax year the corporation exists, and a holding corporation exists until it is dissolved. Holding nothing, trading nothing and banking nothing changes what goes in the return, not whether it is due.

No. A dividend received is income to the holding corporation, so the year is not nil and the return is a full T2 with income to report. That is handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca for $350.00 plus HST per year.

It can be, where the shares paid nothing. Holding an asset is not income by itself. The year stops being nil the moment the operating company pays a dividend, the holding corporation earns interest, or anything is sold.

Schedules 100, 125, 141 and 50 in almost every case, plus Schedule 24 on the first return after incorporation. Schedule 8 is filed only where the corporation owns depreciable property. The table above sets out each one and when it applies.

Rarely. The exemption is for a corporation with genuinely nothing to report, and a holding corporation has a balance sheet by definition. Share capital, a shareholder loan or the shares it holds all put figures on Schedule 100, which makes Schedules 125 and 141 required with it.
There is no cap. Each year is a separate T2 at $300.00 plus HST per tax year with its own T183CORP, and they are filed oldest first so the balance sheet carries forward correctly.

No. The number is the legal name. The return carries the corporation name exactly as the registry holds it, which for a numbered corporation is the number followed by the legislation it was incorporated under.

The year stays open indefinitely. The Canada Revenue Agency can issue a demand to file and then assess the corporation arbitrarily, and an unfiled year blocks the clearance certificate needed to dissolve. Filing the outstanding returns is what closes it.

Once per tax year. Each year is a separate return with its own transmission, so a corporation filing five unfiled years signs five T183CORP forms. All of them can be signed electronically in one sitting.

The final T2 is due within six months of the date of dissolution, and every earlier year has to be filed before a clearance certificate will be issued. Nil years in that run are filed at the same $300.00 plus HST per tax year.
